web/blobs/service.py:R6:_atomic_write_bl: `except OSError as rollback_exc:` is the ROLLBACK arm nested inside `except BaseException as guard_exc:`, and the enclosing handler's body ends in a bare `raise` that re-raises `guard_exc` - so nothing is swallowed; the rule's `_handler_is_silent` inspects only the inner handler's own body and cannot see that outer `raise`. What is caught: a Tier-3 filesystem fault (`storage.unlink` / `os.unlink(dir_fd=...)` / `_fsync_parent_directory` / `os.fsync(directory_fd)`) raised while removing a fork blob that was published by `os.replace` an instant before `write_guard()` (`_ForkCopyWriteAuthority.require`) reported lease loss with `BlobForkFenceLostError`. The primary signal is that lease loss - it is what tells the fork copier it no longer owns the target session - and letting the secondary OSError escape here would REPLACE it, sending the takeover worker and the operator after the wrong cause. Instead the handler records the residue on the primary via `guard_exc.add_note('Rollback failed: could not remove fork blob published after lease loss ...')` and the outer `raise` carries both. The blob is never left silently 'stored': either the unlink succeeded (no note, file gone) or the note names the published path for reconciliation, and the `finally` still removes the temp artifact. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestBlobRollbackNotes::test_atomic_write_rolls_back_blob_published_before_lease_loss` (rollback succeeds, primary re-raised unchanged, file gone) and `::test_atomic_write_rollback_failure_annotates_lease_loss_and_reraises_it` (rollback fsync raises OSError -> primary `BlobForkFenceLostError` re-raised with exactly one 'Rollback failed' note naming the OSError).
web/blobs/service.py:R6:_restore_staged_: `except OSError as rollback_exc:` annotates the PRIMARY failure it was handed - `primary_exc.add_note('Rollback failed: could not restore deleted blob file ... Blob row and storage may now diverge; manual reconciliation required.')` - and every caller invokes this helper from inside `except BaseException as primary_exc:` and immediately `raise`s: `_stage_blob_deletion` (tombstone fsync failure), `BlobServiceImpl._delete_blob_row_locked` (row delete failure), `BlobServiceImpl.delete_blob` `_sync` (`restore_uncommitted_stage`), and `BlobServiceImpl.cleanup_blobs_for_fork` `_sync`. The helper itself returns None by contract and has no outcome of its own to report; the outcome is the primary exception, which always propagates. The caught OSError is Tier-3 filesystem state during compensation: `os.replace(tombstone, storage)` / `_fsync_parent_directory`, plus the helper's own `FileExistsError` refusing to overwrite replacement content that arrived at `stage.storage` while the delete was in flight (restoring over it would silently corrupt a newer blob). Re-raising the OSError would mask the SQL/commit failure that triggered the rollback; swallowing it silently would hide a row/bytes divergence - the note is the explicit third outcome. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestBlobRollbackNotes::test_restore_staged_deletion_restores_tombstone_without_note` and `::test_restore_staged_deletion_refuses_to_overwrite_replacement_and_annotates_primary` (direct), and end-to-end by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestDeleteBlob::test_delete_blob_sql_failure_restores_file_before_stage_escapes` and `::test_delete_blob_staging_fsync_failure_restores_file_before_stage_escapes`.
web/blobs/service.py:R7:_await_fork_copy: `with suppress(BaseException): await operation_task` in the `except asyncio.CancelledError:` arm around `asyncio.wait({operation_task})`. This coroutine was itself cancelled; the handler first publishes lease loss (`write_authority.lose()`, so the worker thread's next `_ForkCopyWriteAuthority.require` raises `BlobForkFenceLostError` at its next bounded mutation seam), cancels the worker task, DRAINS it so the thread has actually stopped mutating the target session before custody can pass to a takeover worker (docstring: 'discard temporary bytes without releasing target-session custody to a takeover worker first'), and then ends in a bare `raise` of the CancelledError. The drained task's own outcome is deliberately not the result: it terminates with `CancelledError`/`BlobForkFenceLostError` by construction, and `BaseException` is needed because `CancelledError` is not an `Exception`. A worker that had published bytes rolls them back inside `_atomic_write_blob`'s guard arm, so no blob reads as stored. The control that keeps this from being a swallow is the `raise` that terminates the handler - the primary cancellation always propagates. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestCopyBlobsForFork::test_copy_aborts_blocked_fsync_when_periodic_checkpoint_loses_fence_and_takeover_retries` and `::test_fail_cleanup_wins_pause_before_persist_and_stale_writer_leaves_no_blob` (the copy task ends in `BlobForkFenceLostError` and the target session holds no blob).

`with suppress(BaseException): await operation_task` in the `except asyncio.CancelledError:` arm around `await checkpoint()`. Same shape and same control as the sibling arm on the `asyncio.wait` call: the lease-renewal checkpoint was cancelled, so the handler publishes lease loss (`write_authority.lose()` -> the worker's `_ForkCopyWriteAuthority.require` raises `BlobForkFenceLostError` at its next seam), cancels and drains the worker so it has stopped touching target-session files, then ends in a bare `raise`. The drain must tolerate `CancelledError`/`BlobForkFenceLostError` from the worker (hence `BaseException`), and its outcome is subordinate to the cancellation being re-raised. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestCopyBlobsForFork::test_copy_checkpoints_while_source_read_is_blocked` (checkpoint runs concurrently with blocked worker I/O) and `::test_copy_aborts_blocked_fsync_when_periodic_checkpoint_loses_fence_and_takeover_retries`.

`with suppress(BaseException): await operation_task` in the `except BaseException:` arm around `await checkpoint()` - the checkpoint FAILED (typically `GuidedOperationFenceLostError`/`BlobForkFenceLostError` from lease renewal, the fence CAS losing to a takeover). The handler publishes lease loss to the guarded writer (`write_authority.lose()`) - or cancels an unguarded task - drains the worker so custody is not released while a thread is mid-write, and then ends in a bare `raise` of the checkpoint failure, which is the outcome the caller (`BlobServiceImpl.copy_blobs_for_fork`) surfaces to the route. The worker's own terminal exception is discarded on purpose: it is the CONSEQUENCE of the lease loss just published (`_ForkCopyWriteAuthority.require` raising at the next seam), not new information, and a published blob is rolled back inside `_atomic_write_blob` before that exception leaves the worker. Control: the `raise` statement ending the handler. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestCopyBlobsForFork::test_copy_aborts_blocked_fsync_when_periodic_checkpoint_loses_fence_and_takeover_retries` (checkpoint raises `BlobForkFenceLostError` while the worker is blocked in fsync; the copy surfaces that error and the takeover succeeds).
`except (BlobError, SQLAlchemyError, OSError) as cleanup_exc:` is the per-blob error ACCUMULATOR of a best-effort compensation loop, not a swallow: it appends `BlobForkCleanupError(blob_id, exc_type, detail)` to `errors`, which is returned as `BlobForkCleanupResult.errors`, an explicit typed outcome the caller consumes - `web/sessions/routes/sessions.py` turns every entry into a `primary_exc.add_note('RecoveryFailed[<exc_type>]: could not delete fork blob ...')` on the fork failure it is compensating. The loop must continue past one blob's failure so the remaining copied blobs are still reclaimed (each iteration runs its own `_blob_phase_transaction`), and a residual row after failure is additionally recorded on `_BLOB_COPY_FORK_ORPHAN_ROWS_COUNTER`. The tuple is deliberately narrow: `AuditIntegrityError` (custody/authorization violations from `_verify_fork_child_custody` and `_require_failed_fork_cleanup_authorization`, overlapping live+cleanup state) is NOT a `BlobError` and propagates, as do programmer bugs; only Tier-3 storage/DB faults and typed blob-domain errors are recorded per blob. Nothing reads as deleted that was not: `deleted_ids.append` sits after the try and is skipped by the handler's `continue`. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestCopyBlobsForFork::test_cleanup_continues_after_item_failure_and_records_residual_metric` (one blob's delete raises OSError -> the other is deleted, one `BlobForkCleanupError` with exc_type 'OSError', orphan counter incremented, failing blob still listed).

`except (SQLAlchemyError, OSError) as residual_check_exc:` guards the residual-row check that runs AFTER a per-blob cleanup failure has already been recorded. If that diagnostic read itself fails (DB/filesystem, Tier-3), the handler appends a second explicit `BlobForkCleanupError` with `exc_type='RecoveryFailed[<type>]'` to the same `errors` accumulator returned as `BlobForkCleanupResult.errors` (and noted by the route as 'RecoveryFailed[...]'), then `continue`s to the next blob. That is the honest outcome: the first entry says the delete failed, the second says we could not even confirm whether a row remains, so the orphan counter is NOT incremented on a guess (`_BLOB_COPY_FORK_ORPHAN_ROWS_COUNTER.add` is reached only when the check succeeded and found a row). Raising here would abort compensation for every remaining blob because one telemetry probe failed; recording it keeps the loop total and the result exhaustive. Pinned by `tests/unit/web/blobs/test_service.py::TestCopyBlobsForFork::test_cleanup_records_recovery_failed_when_residual_check_cannot_run` (delete raises OSError, the next `_blob_phase_transaction` raises OSError -> two error entries for the blob, exc_types 'OSError' then 'RecoveryFailed[OSError]', no orphan metric, blob still listed).
